sapience_notes.subject: lake-build-guard.sh takes only `build` as its build-mode subcommand; the lake verb goes after `--`
sapience_notes.value: `lake-build-guard.sh test --timeout 1800 -- test` exits 77 (usage error) and prints the usage block. The guard's subcommands are status/preflight/build/result; `build` is the only one that wraps a lake invocation, and the lake verb is the first element of the argument vector after `--`. The correct form for a guarded test run is `lake-build-guard.sh build --timeout 1800 -- test`. The guard validates that vector's head against an allowlist and refuses an unrecognized one BEFORE launching anything, so the mistake is cheap but silent about the fix.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh's narrowed battery does not reach readme-lint.sh even when README files are in the touched set
sapience_notes.value: Measured on BimodalLogic: verify-touched.sh resolved 127 touched paths including three README.md files inside the task's own commits, and mapped none of them to any readme-lint suite. A phase whose verification criterion names readme-lint must therefore invoke scripts/readme-lint.sh directly under the dispatch directive's UNMAPPABLE CRITERION carve-out. readme-lint.sh also exposes no path-scoping flag, so that direct invocation necessarily runs repo-wide.

sapience_notes.subject: readme-lint.sh does not label which stale rows are new; the new set must be computed by differencing against the baseline file
sapience_notes.value: The script prints every live `STALE DATE:` row undifferentiated and reports only a count in its RESULT line (`FAIL (4 new stale dates, 0 new missing dates)`). To name the four, extract the live row paths and `comm -23` them against the paths in scripts/readme-date-baseline.txt. On BimodalLogic this gave 65 live against 63 baseline rows. The script does separately print `PRUNE:` candidates for baseline rows no longer matching a live finding.

sapience_notes.subject: A .claude/-resident test suite failure is structurally unattributable to a repository task in a deploy-boundary repo
sapience_notes.value: In BimodalLogic, .gitignore:107 ignores /.claude entirely, so every file under .claude/scripts/tests/ is untracked. A suite failing there is byte-identical before and after a task's commits and cannot have been caused by them — a stronger argument than 'the paths look unrelated'. Check `git check-ignore -v` on the suite path before spending effort attributing such a failure; combine with a `git show --name-only` sweep over the task's commits showing no .claude/, scripts/ or lib/ path.

sapience_notes.subject: A git-grep axiom-count baseline computed with glob pathspecs silently undercounts against a grep -r over resolved source roots
sapience_notes.value: Comparing `grep -rn '^axiom '` over lean-src-roots.sh's resolved roots (14) against `git grep -c '^axiom ' <base> -- 'FormalSystem/**.lean' ...` (12) produced a false +2 regression signal. The glob pathspecs missed top-level root files like FormalSystem.lean. Always compute both sides with the SAME mechanism — git grep at both revisions over the same literal root list — before reporting an axiom-count delta.

sapience_notes.subject: Regenerating a git-HEAD-stamped generated file on the merged tree fixes the stamp and its counts in one run
sapience_notes.value: typst/generated/status.typ records a stamp-commit from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`. When it was regenerated while HEAD sat on another branch with the contribution's files only in the working tree, the stamp named a commit whose tree could not reproduce the recorded counts. A single bare run of scripts/typst-status-counts.sh on the merged tree repaired both, and the fix is verifiable independently of any gate: `git worktree add --detach <scratch> <stamp-commit>` then `<scratch>/scripts/typst-status-counts.sh --json` (the --json path reads no .lake and takes no lock). typst-sync-check.sh cannot do this job — its Check 2 excludes the stamp fields and compares against the working tree, so it prints 'Nothing to fix' for a stale stamp whose counts already match.

sapience_notes.subject: A pre-fix failure message embedding a metavariable number cannot be pinned with #guard_msgs
sapience_notes.value: The instance-synthesis ordering regression in applyDerivationProof fails pre-fix with `lapply could not synthesize the required instance FrameTag ?fc` — the `?m.N` / `?fc` token is not stable across elaborations, so a #guard_msgs pin on it is unreliable. The stable form is a POSITIVE example that compiles under the fixed ordering, with the pre-fix behaviour hand-verified once (reinstate the old ordering, rebuild, observe, restore the file byte-identically and confirm with `diff -q`) and recorded in a comment so a future reader knows what the example guards.

sapience_notes.subject: A hand-written description column inside generated README fences survives regeneration, so a wrong description is invisible to the invariants check
sapience_notes.value: scripts/check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory carries the description column across verbatim when it regenerates a module inventory table. A stale or placeholder description (`<!-- TODO: add description -->`) therefore never trips `--emit-inventory --check` and stays wrong indefinitely until edited by hand. A hand edit inside the BEGIN GENERATED fences is the sanctioned fix and survives the next regeneration.
